name: Chicken Biryani
cuisine: Hyderabadi-style dum biryani (Mughlai / Deccan; eaten across India, a Mumbai delivery favourite)
equipment: Small heavy-bottomed pot or handi with a tight lid (1.5–2 litre)
Large saucepan for boiling the rice (any pot that holds 1 litre of water)
Flat tawa (griddle) to put under the pot during dum
Frying pan or kadai for the onions (or fry them in the biryani pot itself and lift them out)
Mixing bowl for the marinade, knife, chopping board, measuring spoons, slotted spoon or spatula
Optional: aluminium foil or atta (wheat) dough to seal the lid

steps.text: Rinse 75 g basmati rice in a bowl with water, swish, drain; repeat 3 times.
steps.visualCue: rinse water runs nearly clear
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl of rinsed rice with clear water
steps.videoShot: hand swirling rice in water, water turning from cloudy to clear

steps.text: Cover the rice with 1 cup water and leave it to soak.
steps.visualCue: grains turn opaque white
steps.videoShot: water poured over the rice, timer set to 30 min

steps.text: Put 180 g chicken pieces in the mixing bowl.
steps.tip: make 1–2 shallow cuts on thick pieces so the marinade gets in.
steps.visualCue: pieces patted dry, no pooled water
steps.videoShot: chicken pieces placed into the bowl

steps.text: Add 50 g curd, 8 g ginger-garlic paste, 2 g red chilli powder, a pinch of turmeric, 3 g biryani masala, 4 g salt and 5 ml lemon juice.
steps.visualCue: all spices sitting on top of the chicken
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl with spices added, before mixing
steps.videoShot: spoons of each spice dropping into the bowl

steps.text: Tear half the mint (2–3 g) and half the coriander over the chicken; add the slit green chilli.
steps.visualCue: green flecks over the chicken
steps.videoShot: herbs being torn in over the bowl

steps.text: Mix with a spoon until every piece is coated.
steps.visualCue: evenly orange-red coating, no white curd streaks
steps.cameraCheck: one coated piece lifted on the spoon
steps.videoShot: spoon turning the chicken in the marinade

steps.text: Cover and leave to marinate.
steps.tip: longer marination (2+ hours) gives softer chicken; refrigerate if longer than 30 min.
steps.visualCue: covered bowl
steps.videoShot: cling film or lid going on the bowl

steps.text: While it marinates, peel the onion and slice it into thin half-moons.
steps.visualCue: slices about 2 mm thick, even
steps.cameraCheck: the sliced onion on the board
steps.videoShot: knife slicing the onion thinly

steps.text: Heat 10 ml oil in the heavy pot on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: oil shimmers; a slice of onion sizzles at once
steps.videoShot: one onion slice sizzling in the oil

steps.text: Add the onion slices and fry, stirring often.
steps.tip: lower the heat once they start browning; they turn from brown to burnt in under a minute.
steps.visualCue: deep golden-brown, crisp at the edges, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: onions going from pale to golden brown (time-lapse feel)

steps.text: Lift out about half the fried onions onto a plate and keep aside (for layering).
steps.visualCue: half the onions on the plate, oil left in the pot
steps.videoShot: slotted spoon lifting onions out

steps.text: Warm 15 ml milk (10 sec in a microwave or in a small bowl over the pot) and drop in the saffron strands.
steps.visualCue: milk turning yellow-orange
steps.videoShot: strands dropped into the milk, colour bleeding out

steps.text: Put 1 litre water on high heat in the saucepan to boil.
steps.visualCue: rolling boil
steps.videoShot: bubbles rising fast

steps.text: Add to the water: 1 bay leaf, 2 cardamom, 2 cloves, the cinnamon piece, 1/2 tsp shahi jeera and 6 g salt.
steps.visualCue: spices rolling in the water; water tastes clearly salty
steps.videoShot: whole spices tipped into the pot

steps.text: Turn the heat under the onion pot back to medium and add the marinated chicken (with all its marinade).
steps.visualCue: loud sizzle
steps.videoShot: chicken tipped into the onions and oil

steps.text: Cook the chicken, stirring every minute or two, uncovered.
steps.visualCue: chicken turns from pink to opaque outside; gravy thickens, oil starts to show at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: the pot, tilted to show the thick gravy
steps.videoShot: spatula turning the chicken in the thick masala

steps.text: Cover the chicken pot and cook on low.
steps.tip: if it looks dry, add 2 tbsp water; the rice needs this moisture to steam.
steps.visualCue: chicken about 80% cooked (a cut piece shows only a little pink near the bone); thick, not dry gravy (about 3–4 tbsp)
steps.cameraCheck: one piece cut open near the bone
steps.videoShot: lid lifted, steam rising, piece cut in half

steps.text: Meanwhile, drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling spiced water.
steps.visualCue: rice sinks, water stops boiling for a moment
steps.videoShot: soaked rice slid into the boiling water

steps.text: Boil the rice uncovered, stirring gently once.
steps.tip: this is the most important step. Overcooked rice turns mushy on dum; start checking at 4 min.
steps.visualCue: grain is longer, bends but still has a hard white dot in the centre when pressed (about 70% cooked)
steps.videoShot: grain squeezed, showing a firm core

steps.text: Drain the rice in the colander straight away.
steps.visualCue: separate, steaming grains
steps.videoShot: rice poured into the colander, steam rising

steps.text: Turn off the heat under the chicken. Scatter the rest of the mint and coriander over the chicken.
steps.visualCue: green layer over the chicken
steps.videoShot: herbs falling on the chicken

steps.text: Spread the drained rice evenly over the chicken; do not press it down.
steps.visualCue: loose, even rice layer covering all the chicken
steps.cameraCheck: top view of the rice layer
steps.videoShot: spoon spreading rice to the edges

steps.text: Drizzle the saffron milk in streaks over the rice.
steps.visualCue: yellow-orange patches on the white rice
steps.videoShot: saffron milk poured in lines

steps.text: Scatter the reserved fried onions on top and drizzle 5 g (1 tsp) ghee over everything.
steps.visualCue: brown onions and shiny ghee spots on top
steps.videoShot: onions sprinkled, ghee drizzled

steps.text: Seal the pot: cover with foil, then put the lid on tight.
steps.visualCue: no gaps at the rim
steps.videoShot: foil pressed around the rim, lid pressed down

steps.text: Heat the tawa on medium for 2 min, put the pot on it, and turn the heat to medium for 3 min.
steps.visualCue: faint steam escaping or a soft sizzle from inside
steps.videoShot: pot placed on the hot tawa

steps.text: Reduce to the lowest flame and leave on dum.
steps.visualCue: strong biryani aroma fills the kitchen
steps.videoShot: knob turned down, timer set to 15 min

steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the pot sealed to rest.
steps.visualCue: none needed; do not open
steps.cameraCheck: the closed pot off the heat
steps.videoShot: hand turning off the stove

steps.text: Open the lid and check the rice and chicken.
steps.tip: rice still firm? Sprinkle 1 tbsp water, reseal and give 5 more min on lowest heat.
steps.visualCue: rice fully cooked, long and separate; chicken white right to the bone with no pink juice
steps.cameraCheck: one piece of chicken cut open near the bone
steps.videoShot: lid lifted, steam cloud, cut piece shown

steps.text: Using a flat spoon, scoop from the side down to the bottom so each serve has rice and chicken.
steps.visualCue: white and saffron rice with masala chicken visible together
steps.videoShot: spoon lifting a full-depth scoop onto the plate

reasons: The home version uses 2 tsp oil and 1 tsp ghee, has good protein (about 38 g) from skinless chicken and curd, and is not deep-fried. It is still high in refined white rice and low in vegetables. Restaurant biryani typically uses much more ghee/oil, deep-fried onions, larger rice portions and more salt, often with a fried side.

researchRating.basis: Biryani has been Swiggy's most-ordered dish for nine years running (83 million orders in 2024, mostly chicken biryani), and Hyderabadi biryani is TasteAtlas's top-rated biryani (4.4) and a top-10 rice dish worldwide. Home cooks praise it widely, but many say it is hard to get right at home (mushy rice, dry chicken).

storage: Cool within 1 hour (cooked rice can grow Bacillus cereus if left warm). Fridge: safe for up to 2 days in a closed container. Freezer: up to 1 month. Reheat: sprinkle 1 tbsp water, cover, and heat until steaming hot all through (microwave 2–3 min, stirring halfway, or covered on low heat in a pan).
leftoverRemix: Biryani egg fried rice. Pick the chicken off the bone and chop it, then toss with the rice in a hot pan with 1 scrambled egg, chopped spring onion and a dash of soy sauce or chilli sauce for an Indo-Chinese twist.
burnOff: about 660 kcal = about 9.4 km of running (70 kg adult, ~70 kcal/km), or about 13 km of brisk walking (est., ~50 kcal/km).
